The one-page guide

Own your practice location without buying it today.

We buy the building. You lease it at fair market rent plus a small premium. A written option at year 5 or year 10 lets you buy at a price set by independent appraisal. Built to forward to a spouse, partner, or accountant. Plainly, with the tradeoffs left in.

The timeline

1

The call. Thirty minutes with the founders. We run your numbers and tell you whether the structure pencils, including if the better answer is buying yourself or staying put.

2

The search. We find the right building, or evaluate the one you’re in. You approve location, space, and numbers before anything is signed.

3

The close. Medre buys the building with our capital and our mortgage. Your lease and your written purchase option are signed the same day. The purchase process is fixed here, before the first rent check.

4

The lease years. You see patients. We own the building, the debt, and the landlord obligations.

5

Year 5 or year 10. Your option becomes exercisable. A right, not an obligation. Three outcomes, all yours to choose:

Buy

Appraisal sets the price. You close. The deed is yours.

Renew

Not ready at year 5. The year 10 option stands as written.

Walk

Let it lapse, finish the lease. No penalty, no mortgage in your name.

The premium

Fair market rent

The anatomy of your rent check. The teal slice is the premium.

The base is fair market rent, the same number any landlord would charge. The premium is a small percentage on top: the price of your written option. You see both numbers, separately, before you sign.

What it buys: no down payment, no personal guarantee, and a path to the deed in writing from day one.

The option

Appraisal, not negotiation. The price is set by independent appraisal at fair market value at the time of sale. The process is in your documents on day one. Neither side gets to move the number.

What you never face is a landlord naming a price because they know you can’t leave.

The tradeoffs, plainly

The premium is real money. If you never exercise, it was the cost of keeping the choice open.

Today’s price is not locked. The appraisal at exercise sets it. If your market rises you pay more; if it softens, less.

Buying yourself can be cheaper. If you have the capital and certainty, do that instead. We’ll say so on the call.

Five terms to interrogate in any purchase option, ours included

Who sets the price  ·  When the valuation happens  ·  What conditions attach  ·  What happens if you pass  ·  Whether it survives a practice sale. Bring your attorney and accountant, and have them read everything. The structure survives scrutiny; that is the point of it.
